title: Nexus tool declaration
description: Schema for *.tool.json files consumed by codegen/generate.py. Each file declares one LLM-facing tool: identity, inputs, runtime properties, and per-provider variance. The C++ category class and method are inferred from the file path (parent folder = class in PascalCase, filename = method as Run<Name>) — no implementation block in the JSON.

$schema.description: Editor hint pointing at this file. Allows VS Code / similar editors to validate the document on save.

name.description: On-disk tool identifier. snake_case. Drives the filename (without .tool.json), the C++ method name (Run<PascalCase(name)>On<Thread>), and the generated header (<name>.gen.h). By default it is also the LLM-facing tool name on the wire — set `wire_name` to override that one axis without renaming the file or the C++ method.

wire_name.description: Optional override for the LLM-facing tool name. When omitted, the wire name equals `name`. Use to expose a PascalCase tool name to the model (e.g. wire_name='Read' for Claude-Code parity) while keeping the on-disk identifier lowercase. Only the schema's `name` field changes — codegen artifacts and dispatcher names continue to derive from `name`.

description.description: Human/LLM-facing description. Shipped on the tool definition; the LLM reads this to decide when to call the tool. Keep concise — long prose belongs in the skill instructions, not here.

skill.description: Skill scope. Tools share the same `skill` value belong to the same skill bucket and activate together when Skill('<name>') fires. Omit (or set to 'always_on') for tools that should be available without skill activation.

inputs.description: Ordered list of tool inputs. Order drives the C++ struct field order and the JSON-Schema 'required' list.

name.description: Field name. snake_case. Becomes both the JSON-Schema property key and the C++ struct field name.

required.description: When true, the field is added to the JSON-Schema `required` list AND the C++ struct uses the bare type. When false (default), the C++ struct wraps the field in std::optional<T>.

description.description: Per-input description. Surfaced on the JSON-Schema property. The LLM reads this to fill in the field correctly.

shape.description: Optional advanced shape declaration for object / array<object> types. Currently supports discriminated-union variants for tools that genuinely need anyOf (rare).

discriminator.description: Field name on each variant that identifies the variant kind.

variants.description: Names of dedicated variant *.tool.json files (in a sibling 'variants/' subdirectory) that declare the per-variant shapes.

output_kind.description: Informational. Hints at the shape of the tool's result. Currently not emitted on the wire (the LLM doesn't need it), but reserved for future structured-output support.

runtime.description: Cross-cutting runtime concerns. Codegen wraps the dispatcher according to these. Timeout is intentionally NOT here — it lives in nexus_web's session-level config (agentLoopConfig.actionTimeoutMs) and is threaded through per-call.

thread.description: Which Chromium thread the implementation runs on. For 'ui'/'io'/'any' the generated trampoline DCHECKs this invariant on entry; the upstream dispatcher (ToolsAdapter) is responsible for posting to the correct thread before invoking. 'ui' is the default — required for browser/tabs/WebContents APIs. 'io' for network/disk-bound work on the IO thread. 'any' for pure-CPU tools. 'thread_pool' is for blocking I/O (filesystem, etc.); no thread DCHECK is emitted — the implementation is expected to post to base::ThreadPool itself (typically via base::ThreadPool::PostTaskAndReplyWithResult with base::MayBlock()).

providers.description: Per-provider variance. Each block is OPTIONAL; missing means the provider takes defaults.

strict.description: Opt into provider-side grammar-constrained sampling (Anthropic 'Strict tool use', OpenAI 'Structured Outputs'). Only set true when the tool's schema is provider-strict-compliant: additionalProperties:false on every nested object, no maxItems/minItems/pattern/format.

input_examples.description: Optional canonical example calls. Surfaced on the wire as Anthropic's `input_examples` (other providers silently drop). Each entry must validate against the tool's `inputs` schema; Anthropic returns 400 on any violation.

prompt.description: Optional per-tool prompt-section content. When present, codegen emits an entry into `prompt_tool_entries.gen.h` consumed by `api/catalog/prompt_section_renderer.cc` to compose the `{{TOOL_CATALOG}}` placeholder content. Tools without a `prompt` block are silently skipped — they remain available on the wire but aren't advertised in the system prompt. Replaces the hand-maintained per-tool prose that pre-Phase-12 lived as constexpr blocks in C++ + a parallel BROWSER_TOOL_NAMES set in TS.

section.description: Which section of the system prompt this tool surfaces in. The renderer composes sections in the order browser-tools → file-shell-tools → task-tracking → skills → parallelism (parallelism is always emitted from a static C++ trailer).

group.description: Optional sub-group label within a section. Browser-tools sub-groups today: 'Navigation' / 'Element interaction' / 'Search' / 'Media' / 'Observation' / 'Termination'. Other sections currently don't subdivide and should omit this field.

line.description: The bullet line shown to the LLM. One or two short sentences naming the tool's signature and intended usage. The renderer prefixes a single '- ' bullet marker — do not include it in the line itself.
